summary: Takashi Yamada worked in sinology and religious studies. He studied at Hosei University and served as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto around 1999.
Takatoshi Ito specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor at Komazawa University, with his tenure attested between 1978 and 1981, as well as in 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and held a researcher post at Taisho University's Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute, attested in 1978.

Takatsugu Hayashi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Delhi (attested 1996). He held posts at Tohoku University (attested 1997), Sendai National College of Technology (attested 2008), and Hosen Gakuen College (attested 2015).

Takayasu Higuchi specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), he became professor there (~1953–1983) and directed the Sen-oku Hakuko Kan and the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Takayasu Kimura worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (1973–1978) and held posts at Taisho University and Shingon Buddhism Buzan-ha in 1995.
Takayasu Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1983 to 1994 and became a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University around 2008.

Takayoshi Kamei worked in history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912), he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Ibaraki University (~1949–1952), and Seisen University (~1950–1968), and taught Hajime Nakamura.

Takayoshi Namikawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning multiple degrees at Bukkyo University between ~1969 and 1996. He became a professor there in 1981 and emeritus professor in 2018, also holding appointments at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Hokkaido University.

Takayuki Hirosawa specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Hamburg under supervisor Lambert Schmithausen. He worked at Taisho University, serving as a group member through 1991 and as professor by 2014.

Takehiro Sueki specialized in philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He held academic posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1952–1969), the University of Tokyo (~1969–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).

Takeo Hibino studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936) and worked in sinology and history/archaeology. He held positions at Kyoto University from 1936 to 1977, followed by professorships at Otemon Gakuin University (1977) and Otemae University (1980), serving as president.

Takeo Kanaseki was a scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held academic posts at Kyushu University (~1950–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1964), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1964–1979).
Takeo Warita is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University and was taught by Giyu Nishi.

Takeshi Fujii specialized in Indology and history/archaeology, studying at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He advanced from assistant to professor (2001, 2009) and emeritus professor (2021) at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Takeshi Karashima specialized in sinology, having studied at Yamaguchi Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University (~1925–1928). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Kamakura's library (~1957–1963), Sagami Women's University, and Showa Women's University.

Takeshi Umehara worked in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies, studying at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan, and Kyoto City University of Arts, later directing the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995).

Takeshiro Kuraishi worked in sinology and linguistics after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He held professorships at Kyoto University (~1939–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and served as president of Chugokugo Gakkai (~1957–1968).

Takezo Kaneko specialized in philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929) under Tetsuro Watsuji. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1966) and held posts at International Christian University, Seikei University, and Hokkaido University.

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé, taught Keith Dowman and Phakchok Rinpoche, and succeeded Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012.
